dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation

evidence.note: Inspected all four graph file headers (sizes), read file format, inspected and validated the reference alignment (all nodes covered, unique valid targets), and recognized the perfect alignment could be copied for y2kr-SC — identifying the NC lever per deliverable.

Named multiple concrete published alignment methods (MAGNA, GHOST, GRAAL, seed-and-extend, SANA) and selected SANA-style simulated annealing with a stated rationale, choosing C for runtime on 7937/13276-node instances.
Quantified a baseline: degree-rank alignment yields S3=0.01, and diagnosed the cause (dense top-degree subgraph inflating E2_aligned).
Computed degree stats (avg ~8.7 vs ~16.6) and derived exact Ea/E2a values required to reach S3=0.32, identifying the precise structural signal the S3 threshold rewards.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent systematically characterized each pair's sizes/format, inspected the reference alignment and exploited it as the per-deliverable NC lever, quantified a concrete baseline (S3=0.01), and derived the exact structural targets for the S3 threshold — matching the level-8 anchor's systematic characterization plus task-specific-lever recognition. It stops short of level 10 because it performed no actual literature/web research, only listed methods before quickly committing to SANA rather than evaluating multiple published methods against runtime, and its degree-distribution analysis was limited to averages.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones

evidence.note: Explicitly separated the two deliverables: recognized y2kr-SC could be solved by verifying+copying the provided perfect alignment, while DM-HS required a real algorithm with S3>=0.32 — distinct per-deliverable sub-goals and effort budgeting by difficulty.

Sequenced pipeline: parse graphs into adjacency sets, produce a baseline degree-rank alignment and MEASURE it (S3=0.01), then decide to build an SA optimizer — baseline-before-optimize ordering with a measured checkpoint.
Built the C scorer computing Ea/E2a/S3 before running optimization; scorer-before-optimize sequencing is present.
Derived numeric done-criteria: algebraically computed the exact Ea (~12,800) needed to reach S3=0.32 given E2a, tying milestone completion to the threshold.

Extended terminal-freeze period with ~85 undifferentiated 'wait' steps and no milestone re-planning; shows the milestone structure was not sustained/adaptive through failure (though partly an environment fault).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly separated parsing, scoring, and alignment generation and tracked the two deliverables distinctly against their own thresholds (anchor 5), and went further: it measured a baseline, built the scorer before optimizing, and derived numeric done-criteria (the Ea needed for S3=0.32), which are core elements of anchor 8, plus it budgeted effort by deliverable difficulty (a level-10 signal — solving yeast trivially via the reference). It falls short of a full 8-10 because the milestones were emergent rather than an explicitly enumerated hierarchy, there were no articulated per-milestone fallback branches or explicit gating, and the long frozen tail showed no milestone-level re-planning. This places it at 7.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics

evidence.note: Validated the perfect y2kr-SC alignment: confirmed full coverage of all 2379 Y2KR nodes, all SC targets valid and unique (injectivity check), correct format — then copied it. NC assumed ≈1.0 by reasoning but never implemented as a scorer.
Caught a real scorer bug: E2a going negative producing a negative denominator and garbage S3; fixed the delta computation. Shows active guarding against edge-set-computation errors.

S3 (Ea, E2a, denominator) implemented inside the SANA optimizer and used directly as the optimization objective; agent back-solved the S3 formula algebraically to determine the Ea/E2a targets needed for S3>=0.32, i.e. used the metric as its stopping/pass test.
At submission the agent trusted SANA's reported S3~0.27 for DM-HS with no independent re-scoring of the final file and no reference-alignment sanity check; NC was never computed for any deliverable.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent implemented S3 faithfully within its optimizer and used it as the optimization objective and pass test (above level 5), debugged a real E2_aligned/denominator bug, and validated injectivity/coverage/format for the yeast deliverable. However it never implemented an NC scorer (relying on the perfect alignment giving NC=1.0 by definition), never scored the reference alignment to sanity-check its S3 code, and built no independent cross-check of the SANA-reported score — falling short of the level-8 anchor's reference-scoring sanity checks. This places it at 6.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization

evidence.note: Tracks current S3 vs the 0.32 target as it climbs (0.1364@30s, 0.18@60s), establishing continuity of best-so-far early.
Detects regression: the 1800s schedule left best at 0.0014, far below the earlier 0.18 run; recognizes the schedule cooled too slowly and reverts.
Quantitative trend/rate reasoning: 'S3 went 0.20@220s to 0.258@820s... 0.058 in 600s... but it's slowing' — distinguishes converging-slowly from stalling.
Repeated explicit plateau detection at ~0.26-0.269 across runs; kills runs when gains stop rather than looping indefinitely.
Computes exact Ea/E2a needed to reach S3=0.32 from current best — precise distance-to-threshold accounting.
Even after terminal froze, retains accurate model: DM-HS ~0.27 (fails 0.32), y2kr-SC perfect (passes) — never loses track of where each deliverable stands.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintains best-so-far per deliverable, does quantitative rate extrapolation and threshold arithmetic, repeatedly recognizes plateaus and a regression, and preserves its best alignment while experimenting — squarely matching the level-8 anchor and touching level-10 traits (logged score progression, converging-vs-stuck distinction). It stops short of 10 because it re-ran the same SA into the identical ~0.26 plateau three times before pivoting, and the long frozen-terminal span left it unable to act on its otherwise accurate monitoring.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met

evidence.note: Degree-rank baseline gave S3≈0.01; agent diagnosed the root cause (high-degree nodes collapsing into a dense HS subgraph) and pivoted to a materially different approach (C-based simulated annealing). A genuine strategy switch prompted by the shortfall.
Diagnosed that the SA cooling schedule was too slow using observed T-vs-progress data, and retuned T_start/T_end deliberately rather than blindly rerunning.
Detected plateau at S3≈0.26, diagnosed it as a local optimum, and built sana2 with restart-from-best/re-heating — a deliberate pivot that keeps accumulated gains.

On a second plateau (~0.267), enumerated concrete alternatives (multi-swap moves, restarts, re-weighted objective), tried a different objective (dEa−0.5·dE2a), tested it, judged it worse, and moved to abandon it — evidence-driven revision and quick abandonment of a dead end.

Terminal froze; ~90 steps of waiting/kill attempts. Planned further pivots (larger moves, multiple restarts) were never executed, and the agent submitted the below-threshold 0.27 file — the adaptation arc was cut off rather than completed.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent repeatedly diagnosed the specific cause of each shortfall (degree-rank collapse, too-slow cooling, local-optimum plateaus) and pivoted deliberately while preserving its best result (restart/re-heat, objective re-weighting, and reverting a failed objective), which matches the level-8 anchor of cause-diagnosis-plus-deliberate-pivot. It stops short of level 10 because it never got to execute most of the alternatives it enumerated (multi-swap moves, multiple restarts) and only combined signals within SA variants, with the final arc curtailed by an unrecoverable terminal freeze. This places observed behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, closer to 8, i.e. a 7.

rubric.task_read: An open-ended global network-alignment optimization task: produce two injective node mappings between PPI networks that clear specified S3 (topological) and NC (node-correctness) thresholds. The horizon is long and the difficulty is real — hitting the numeric targets likely requires researching/implementing a nontrivial alignment algorithm (e.g., seed-and-extend, IsoRank/SANA/MAGNA-style), plus building the S3/NC metrics locally since the metrics are fully specified but the grader is hidden. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in research, self-verification, and iterative optimization; the two deliverables have different constraints (one needs NC against a provided reference), so approaches may diverge.

dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation
dimensions.description: Inspecting the graph files/sizes and the reference alignment, and researching/selecting a suitable network-alignment approach before committing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: S3/NC thresholds are hard to hit with a naive mapping; the space of alignment algorithms is well-studied, and the provided reference alignment plus node-name overlap are exploitable signals. Acting blind almost guarantees thrash.

anchors.0: Starts writing a mapping with no look at graph sizes, file format, or the reference alignment; no consideration of what algorithm could work.
anchors.3: Skims one file and picks an arbitrary heuristic (e.g., degree-sort or random injective map) without weighing whether it can clear the thresholds.
anchors.5: Reads both network pairs (sizes, format, node-name conventions), inspects the reference alignment, and picks a known-reasonable approach (seed-and-extend, IsoRank, or an existing tool) with a stated rationale.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes each pair (|V|,|E|, degree distribution, shared node names), researches concrete alignment methods and their fit to S3 vs NC, and notices task-specific levers (name-overlap for NC, topology for S3; differing constraints per deliverable) that shape the plan.
anchors.10: Deep, sustained orientation: quantifies what score a baseline achieves, identifies the exact structural signal each threshold rewards, evaluates multiple published methods against the concrete instance sizes/runtime, and derives a targeted strategy per deliverable grounded in that analysis.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into ordered sub-goals (parse → metric implementation → baseline alignment → optimization) each with a concrete done-check tied to the score thresholds.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Two deliverables with distinct constraints and a multi-stage pipeline mean undifferentiated 'just write the file' effort will strand the agent without knowing whether it's close.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push; no separable stages, no per-deliverable structure.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering only; treats both alignments as one blob and has no notion of intermediate checkpoints.
anchors.5: Separates parsing, scoring, and alignment generation, and tracks the two deliverables distinctly with their respective thresholds as goals.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones (parser verified → S3/NC computable → baseline score measured → optimize to threshold) each with a numeric done-criterion, sequenced sensibly (e.g., build the scorer before optimizing against it).
anchors.10: A crisp milestone hierarchy that also budgets effort across the two deliverables by difficulty (the NC-constrained yeast task vs the S3-only fly task), with fallback branches per milestone and clear gating on measured scores before advancing.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics
dimensions.description: Building/using a correct local implementation of S3 and NC (and injectivity/format checks) to measure alignments before trusting them.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader is hidden but the metrics are fully specified. An agent that cannot compute its own S3/NC is optimizing blind and cannot know if it passed; a subtly wrong scorer is worse than none.

anchors.0: Never computes S3 or NC; submits alignments hoping they pass.
anchors.3: Eyeballs coverage or computes a rough proxy, but no faithful S3/NC implementation; no format/injectivity validation.
anchors.5: Implements S3 and NC per the spec and runs them on its alignments, plus checks injectivity, full coverage of V1, and exact node-name/format matching.
anchors.8: Faithful metric implementation that it sanity-checks (e.g., scores the reference alignment to confirm NC≈1.0 and a sensible S3, tests edge cases like the E2_aligned denominator), and uses the score as the optimization objective/stopping test.
anchors.10: Rigorously validated scorer used as a tight feedback loop: cross-checks the S3 formula against the reference, guards against off-by-one/edge-set-double-counting bugs, verifies format matches the exact spec, and treats a passing local score as necessary-but-scrutinized rather than final.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of current S3/NC vs targets across iterations and detecting stalled or plateaued optimization.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Optimization can plateau below threshold; without tracking best-so-far scores the agent won't know if it's converging, stuck, or regressing across a long run.

anchors.0: No awareness of current scores or distance to thresholds; can't say whether it's improving.
anchors.3: Occasionally prints a number but no continuity — no sense of best-so-far or trend.
anchors.5: Tracks current S3/NC against each threshold and knows which deliverables still fall short.
anchors.8: Maintains best-so-far per deliverable across iterations, recognizes plateaus/regressions, and decides when an approach has stopped yielding gains rather than looping indefinitely.
anchors.10: Disciplined trajectory monitoring: logs score progression, distinguishes 'converging slowly' from 'stuck', avoids re-running variants that already failed, and preserves the best alignment while exploring — never loses the plot over a long optimization horizon.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met
dimensions.description: Changing algorithm, parameters, or signal (topology vs name-overlap vs reference-seeding) when the current approach plateaus below target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A first-choice method may not reach S3≥0.55/NC≥0.30; success often depends on switching or combining strategies rather than grinding the same one.

anchors.0: Keeps the same failing approach (or ships a below-threshold file) despite no progress.
anchors.3: Minor tweaks only (reruns with a different seed) without diagnosing why it fell short.
anchors.5: When stuck, tries a materially different tactic (new algorithm, added seeding, tuned objective) prompted by the observed shortfall.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the cause of the shortfall (e.g., NC low → exploit name-overlap/reference seeding; S3 low → local topological search) and pivots deliberately, keeping what worked.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven course-correction: forms hypotheses about why a metric lags, tests targeted changes, combines complementary signals for the two different constraint sets, and abandons dead ends quickly without discarding accumulated gains.
